links.outcome: Guideline-concordant ACS management recommendations when varying patient gender and race in prompts
links.effect: Specifying patients as female, African American, or Hispanic decreased guideline-recommended medical management, diagnosis, and symptom management; largest disparities in angiography/stress testing and high-intensity statins.
links.quote: We find that specifying patients as female, African American, or Hispanic resulted in a decrease in guideline recommended medical management, diagnosis, and symptom management of ACS.

unlisted_practices: Prompting the LLM to explain its reasoning before answering (chain-of-thought) to improve accuracy and mitigate gender and racial bias

screen.reason: Empirical evaluation of ChatGPT 3.5 on clinical vignettes of acute coronary syndrome, demonstrating demographic biases and testing whether a prompt engineering safeguard (asking the model to explain its reasoning first) mitigates these biases.

primary.practice: chain-of-thought prompt engineering (explain reasoning prior to answering)
